A refund was requested by email and initially approved, but the company required the return shipment to be sent to China — contradicting their stated U.S. location.
After the merchandise was shipped back at a personal cost of $85, the buyer attempted to send proof of return and the tracking number to the same email previously used for correspondence. The email address had suddenly become invalid. The company continues to operate online, but its contact email no longer works, and there is no confirmation that the refund will ever be issued. These behaviors — false business location, poor-quality goods, shifting return requirements, and disappearing communication — strongly indicate that Harper & Wells is operating as a fraudulent company. Do not buy from it.
